d: Understand fundamentals of design that help prevent cheaters and exploiters from ruining the playing experience.
h:
The following content covers various concepts and tactics to improve security and mitigate cheating in your Roblox games. It's highly recommended that all developers read through these to ensure that your games are secure and fair for all users. Check the sidebar for additional security topics.

Basic design decisions can serve as "first step" security measures to discourage exploits. The core principle is to design systems where cheating is either impossible or provides no meaningful advantage, rather than trying to detect and prevent cheating after the fact.

Consider a shooter game where players earn points for kills. An exploiter might create bots that teleport to the same location to be repeatedly killed for easy points. This scenario illustrates the difference between reactive and defensive approaches:

Approach Predictable outcome
Chase down bots by writing code that attempts to detect them (reactive approach).
Exploiters seeking quick points will find a way around your complex detection code and use their bots in a different way.
Reduce or outright remove point gains for kills on newly spawned players (defensive approach).
Extra time and friction is now required for exploiters because they get no points for instantly killing their bots. Additionally, "spawn campers" are discouraged because they no longer get points for killing newly spawned players.

Additional defensive design scenarios:

Potential exploit scenario Reactive Approach (less effective) Defensive approach (more effective)
(Obby) Exploiter teleports to the end to claim rewards Only check the player's final position and try to detect impossible completion times Design with mandatory, sequential checkpoints. Server validates each checkpoint was activated in order before granting rewardsYou can add another layer by flagging players who complete stages faster than humanly possible. The design of the game (requiring checkpoints) is what enables the effective server-side validation.
(Combat) Client reports dealing impossible damage amounts Try to detect and filter out impossible damage values Server calculates all damage from server-sided weapon stats and validates hits through server-side raycasting
(Economy) Exploiter duplicates items through rapid requests Try to detect duplicate requests or unusual patterns Implement server-side cooldowns and validate all transactions against current player inventory state

Key principle
When designing a new feature, ask yourself: "How would an exploiter abuse this, and can I change the design to make that abuse impossible or worthless?" Instead of trying to detect cheating after it happens, design your game so that cheating either cannot occur or provides no meaningful advantage.

kid.simple: Instead of chasing cheaters after they cheat, you can design your game so cheating does not work or is not worth it. This is called defensive design. It is often easier and stronger than writing tricky code to catch cheaters. Before adding a feature, ask how a cheater could abuse it, and change the design so that abuse fails.
kid.analogy: Rather than hiring a guard to catch people sneaking cookies, you put the cookie jar in a locked cupboard. You stop the problem by how you set things up, not by catching people afterward.
keyPoints: Reactive means trying to catch cheating after it happens. Defensive means designing so cheating cannot happen or gives no reward.
Cheaters usually find a way around detection code, so defensive design works better.
Shooter example: give fewer or no points for killing players who just spawned. Bot farms stop paying off, and spawn camping is discouraged too.
Obby example: make players touch checkpoints in order, and have the server check the order before giving rewards.
Combat example: the server works out damage from its own weapon stats and checks hits with its own raycasts.
Economy example: add server-side cooldowns and check every trade against the player's real inventory, so spamming requests cannot copy items.
Key question for every feature: how would a cheater abuse this, and can I change the design so that abuse is impossible or worthless?

terms.exploit: A way of cheating by abusing a weakness in the game.
terms.reactive approach: Waiting for cheating to happen, then trying to spot and stop it.
terms.defensive approach: Building the game so cheating cannot work or gives nothing useful.
terms.bot: A fake or computer-controlled player account a cheater uses, for example to get killed over and over for free points.
terms.spawn camping: Waiting near where players appear and attacking them right away.
terms.checkpoint: A spot in an obby that saves your progress. Required checkpoints in order prove the player really went through the level.
terms.server-side: Done on Roblox's server, where cheaters cannot change the code.
terms.cooldown: A wait time before you can do the same action again, like 1 second between purchases.
terms.raycasting: Shooting an invisible line from one point to see what it hits. The server can use it to check if a shot really hit.
terms.friction: Here it means extra effort or hassle that makes cheating less worth it.

example.title: Checkpoints that must be touched in order
example.place: Script in ServerScriptService (add Parts named Checkpoint1, Checkpoint2, Checkpoint3 to a Folder named Checkpoints in Workspace)
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")

local checkpoints = Workspace:WaitForChild("Checkpoints")
local TOTAL = 3

-- The server remembers the last checkpoint each player reached
local progress = {}

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	progress[player] = 0
end)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	progress[player] = nil
end)

for i = 1, TOTAL do
	local part = checkpoints:WaitForChild("Checkpoint" .. i)
	part.Touched:Connect(function(hit)
		local player = Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent)
		if not player or progress[player] == nil then
			return
		end
		-- Only count this checkpoint if it is the very next one
		if progress[player] == i - 1 then
			progress[player] = i
			print(player.Name, "reached checkpoint", i)
			if i == TOTAL then
				print(player.Name, "finished the obby! Give reward here.")
			end
		end
	end)
end
explain: The server stores each player's progress as a number, starting at 0.
Each checkpoint part listens for touches.
A touch only counts if it is the next checkpoint in order. Touching checkpoint 3 while at 0 does nothing.
The reward only happens after the last checkpoint, so teleporting straight to the end earns nothing.

watchOut: Only checking a player's final position for rewards. A teleporting cheater passes that check easily.
Trusting damage numbers sent by the client. Keep weapon stats on the server and calculate damage there.
Letting players spam buy or trade requests. Add a server cooldown and check the real inventory each time.
Spending a lot of time on detection code first. Try changing the design before writing detectors.
